notes: Standard: as in the 2026-10-31-b and 2026-10-31 grades, a problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it. A silent fix, or a mention only under behaviour changes or assumptions, does not count, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported. The mapping is the same: the nesting belongs to 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; the comments, both magic numbers and a dropped line 11 comment to 'Comments explain why...'; input lines 12 and 55 to the pipeline rule; the line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors to 'Match every expected shape...'; the line 8 raise and the `try/rescue` with `String.to_integer/1` to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; the dead `is_binary` to no rule. git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes two places: 'Match every expected shape...' now states the different-reasons sentence the standard already applied, and the `with` rule gains a sentence outside this list. So no verdict moves.

Magic 18, the most common miss: eight of nine runs break 'Comments explain why...' through it. Ajuyu, fhdvv, gqyen and jffjh name it `@min_age` silently; gtstz, qhbfs and wsyha keep the literal and name it nowhere. Hgrgw reports it (finding 12). Egebh is the close call: finding 16 calls the 18 magic, so it counts as reported and egebh reaches 21 of 21, but the companion changeset the review shows keeps `greater_than_or_equal_to: 18` (line 147), so the rule is violated. This follows the case file's 2026-10-22 ba24972 Haiku entry, whose changeset sketch kept the `18` it called magic. It differs from 2026-10-31-b's haiku-2 only because that run's changeset was assumed and not shown, so no literal was in its code.
The 120 counts in all nine through a fix or finding that names `@max_age`, as the standard held for its sonnets. None uses `min(age, 120)` in a finding's fix.

Gtstz nesting, borderline: the only mention is the last sentence of finding 5, 'The nested `if` blocks go away with it.' A finding names it, and it is not under behaviour changes, so it counts, and 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...' are clean. Held the other way, gtstz would be 17 of 21 and both rules would be violated.

Gtstz `&&`: finding 9 applies the operator rule only to line 27, and finding 5 quotes line 21 only as a hand-written check. So the line 21 `&&` is missed and the rule is violated, as the case file held for the 2026-10-21 Sonnet run that applied this rule only to the must-not-report line. Gtstz is the only run where this flips the rule.

Gqyen false positive, borderline: finding 10's title says '`&&` and `!` on booleans (line 21)'. The `!` occurs only on line 27, which is how 2026-10-31-b counted its sonnet-1, so it is listed; the finding's own line number points the other way. No verdict depends on it.

Gqyen closure copy: finding 15 does not name the copy, but its stated fix ends 'with the message built first', which addresses it, the test 2026-10-31 applied to haiku-2 and b applied to haiku-1. Jffjh's finding 16 has no such clause, so its copy is unreported and line 121 is a silent fix.

Line 8 raise: all nine count. Egebh ('A missing role also raises on `nil`.'), jffjh ('a `nil` role raises'), qhbfs ('and raises on `nil`.') and wsyha ('A missing role raises `ArgumentError`.') do not mention the `try`, but b counted the same wording for its sonnets.

Identical errors: hgrgw's finding 6, qhbfs's finding 9, wsyha's finding 6 and egebh's finding 6 each compare distinct failures, so they count. Gtstz's finding 2 treats the rescue only as hiding failures and its line 143 is under behaviour changes, so it does not.
Qhbfs line 12: finding 13's 'one-step pipeline of string concatenation' describes input lines 54-55, not `params["email"] |> String.downcase()`, so input line 12 is unreported.

Catch-alls in the improved code: a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted, as 2026-10-31 held (ajuyu line 102, egebh line 105, fhdvv line 105, gtstz line 102, hgrgw line 92). Hgrgw line 118 `_ -> changeset` passes the changeset through over an open set of constraints. Ajuyu line 120 `defp maybe_notify(_user, _notify), do: :ok` is the close call: it silently ignores a stale `notify: true`, which is against the heading, but the rule's sentences are about result shapes and the standard counts only input line 33 and the identical errors, so ajuyu stays clean. A stricter reading would mark it violated. Gqyen's missing role returns `{:unknown_role, nil}` (line 67 with line 82); the clause names what it caught, so it is not counted.

Line 27 and line 19 false positives: ajuyu, egebh, gtstz, qhbfs and wsyha put line 27 under the operator rule, gqyen does so borderline, and jffjh's finding 11 lists line 19. Fhdvv and hgrgw have none. Every run keeps the line 11 why-comment (ajuyu line 81, egebh 84, fhdvv 98, gqyen 85, gtstz 75, hgrgw 82, jffjh 91, qhbfs 105, wsyha 90). Non-planted findings on lines outside the must-not-report table, such as wsyha's alias split and egebh's Mailer note, are not false positives.

Required keys: fhdvv is the only violation, from `Map.get/2` on a struct, its own stated fix for `user[:name]`. Ajuyu's and gtstz's `opts[:notify]` read options whose default is documented, as 2026-10-31 accepted. Body reads of string keys are not counted.
